longs.thesis: Bloomberg reported Samsung Electronics is in talks to acquire the data-center cooling maker; neither company has confirmed, no price or terms reported. Gapping far above the prior day's high on deal-premium expectations, reclaiming the ~15% slide since its Nov 3 earnings miss.

Q3 revenue $3.46M beat the ~$2.0M estimate (+58% sequentially) and a new $8.9M USSOCOM task order moves the C-130J autonomy program into integration. Beaten-down microcap gapping off a Nov 5 52-week low ($0.74), still ~81% below its 200-day.

Surprise Q3 profit (adjusted +$29.8M vs a $38.4M loss expected) and raised 2026 revenue forecast to $940-960M; cloud/services revenue more than tripled on the OpenAI deal, Microsoft signed as a customer. Deep drawdown name (down 47.2% from its May IPO price) gapping on a clean raise.
Q3 swung to a $15.2M profit ($0.12/share) from a $4.1M loss a year ago; revenue +52.5% to $69.0M. Thin premarket volume (~6.2k shares), so the print is fragile.

Giving back Thursday's +175.6% regular-session surge on continued EV micro-cap weakness and dilution fears. A one-day parabolic move unwinding - the fade side of yesterday's top gainer.
